review: The modeled shelter sits on the approximate apron inferred from historical aerial images and the retained path edge. The conservation account and current photos support this site. The inscription faces south. Canopy obscures the exact roof outline and footings. Fine inscriptions, rafter dimensions and apron width are estimates.

overheadReview.basis: This mosaic covers the west-side draft and the mapped Silkworm Deity Temple. The earlier zoom-20 mosaic was centered on the east-side trial and stopped short of these points.
overheadReview.finding: The temple roof is visible. The draft and three nearby west-side trial points fall under canopy or shadow. The image offers no distinguishable shelter ridge or path junction for registering a precise center.

groundReference.note: The round-headed tablet and paired planter pockets identify the monument. The photo shows its paving and capped stone boundary wall. The publisher reused a photo of unknown date.

secondaryOverheadReview.finding: The temple roof and a roughly north–south walk in the west-side search corridor are distinguishable. Branches and shadows cover the trial area. The wall and shelter in the ground photos cannot be identified together in the aerial view.

archivedOverheadReview.scope: Esri imagery west of the mapped Silkworm Deity Temple. Labels are archive release dates.
archivedOverheadReview.note: The six Wayback releases were compared at the same tile coordinates. The higher-contrast 2023 view distinguishes the Silkworm Deity Temple and a path farther west. Across both leafy and less leafy views the immediate path beside the shelter and the shelter footprint cannot be picked out as a reliable match. The west-side draft remains provisional.

imagery.fit: The exposed section is in the western garden. The nearest visible path segment runs roughly north to south and is west of the former draft pin. The photographs show the approach beside the east apron. The segment could be a continuation or neighboring path under the canopy.

entry.title: Summer Palace · Farming and Weaving Stele
entry.note: Draft trial 18 m west and 2 m north of the mapped Silkworm Deity Temple. A 2022 visitor account places the temple east of the stele. The shelter itself is obscured by trees, so the offset and ground elevation remain provisional. The stele faces south per the Palace Museum description.

nativeTrial.note: Both photos show a nearly north–south walk beside the shelter. The extended paving clears the ten terrain and landcover probes at street and close range. The PMTiles extract has no matching local walk, and no mapped footprint intersects the trial. The shelter anchor and grade remain unverified.

entry.title: Summer Palace · Farming and Weaving Stele
entry.note: Approximate, south-facing placement on the archival apron beside the west garden walk. The conservation account and photographs support adding the shelter over the same stele. The terrain-relative offset fits the paving to the sampled surface. Canopy limits absolute placement accuracy.

terrainReference.basis: Terrarium ground at the apron center meets the model at the recorded local height.

previousTerrainRelativeTrial.limitations: Synthetic shifts test vertical offsets with the same slope. Local slope differences and the actual footing remain unverified.

entry.title: Summer Palace · Farming and Weaving Stele
entry.note: Draft beside the west garden walk, about 37 m west of the Silkworm Deity Temple. The south-facing title follows the exposed path segment. The model uses the terrain at its own anchor. Canopy obscures the physical shelter and the approach junction.

terrainReference.basis: Terrarium height at the west-walk draft anchor, referenced to the calibrated paving clearance.

interpretationSign.notes: The rounded bronze-toned sign has a stepped metal lip, two round posts, concealed gaps between the mounting points and turned caps. The inscription is too small to transcribe from the reference photographs.

shelterPhotoReview.observation: The street and close-up roofs use layered hip caps with curled corners and upturned ends on the main ridge. The close-up roof retains the rounded tile courses and painted rafter ends. The curved trim follows the photographed shelter and reuses the shared fired-clay material.

wallControl.projectionBasis: Eight wall-ground contact points projected from the photographed post geometry onto an estimated local plane. This is a relative bearing.

railingPhotoReview.observation: The south railing plaque carries two introductory lines and the two photo-traced poem columns beneath its seven-character heading. The master and close-up tiers show this fine detail on the shared painted-metal surface. The shelter retains round rails and curled clay roof trim.

images.observation: A red courtyard gate, a white wall and an exposed irregular stone occupy the same frame.
The irregular stone has several columns of smaller writing and a straight stepped plinth. Its profile differs from the rounded, three-character tablet and wave-carved base.

rejectedListing.scope: The listing’s photo set does not establish a location or bearing for the modeled stele.

openApronComparison.observation: The open-apron photo shows the round-headed title stone, the wave plinth, bronze guardrails and an irregular stone wall with dark coping. The sheltered front photo shows the same wall construction west of the pavilion. The wall supports the local orientation inferred from the photos. Its position is unresolved in the overhead imagery.

plaquePoems.observation: The bronze railing plaque separates a seven-character heading from two introductory lines and its left and right poem columns. The close-up mesh uses a simplified trace of the ink below the rule. The contact footer is outside the crop.

walkSequence.observation: The photographer reports turning back from the stele to reach Fortress Lake. The park sign shows a map pin at the lake path junction. The sequence relates the stele to the temple and path junction without showing the connecting walk in a single frame.

evidence.observation: The three images show a dark rectangular object on a square pale apron attached to the west side of a garden path. The canal works and Silkworm Deity Temple lie on either side of the garden. The 2005 image is offset and is compared after translating by three canal-lock control points. Tree cover and historical image offsets leave residual positional uncertainty.
evidence.coordinateBasis: June 2009 imagery cursor readout 39°59′41.21″N, 116°15′28.05″E at the center of the dark object on the apron. The absolute image registration and visual pick are approximate.

heading.label: south-facing title
heading.scope: Approximate compass orientation from the Palace Museum description and the narrow east-side garden walk.

historicApronComparison.recentObservation: The approach and canal works remain visible. The open apron area is under branches and shadow. This view does not establish the exact center of the later sheltered state.

testedPose.title: Summer Palace · Farming and Weaving Stele
testedPose.note: Provisional modern shelter trial at the archival open apron. Canopy prevents a direct fit to the modern roof.

historicApronComparison.note: A second trial at the archival apron 12.54 m north of the draft clears terrain and landcover at all ten paving probes per detail level. Recent canopy obscures the roof and wall. The present shelter location remains provisional.

formerDraftNativeTrial.note: The stele and the Silkworm Deity Temple render at the draft pose with the retained PMTiles features and terrain. All ten paving probes clear the ground at street and close range. The inscription faces south and the photographs place the walk to its east. Canopy obscures the shelter and the exact walk junction, so absolute placement remains provisional.

placement.title: Summer Palace · Farming and Weaving Stele
placement.note: Draft on the west side of the exposed garden walk, about 37 m west of the Silkworm Deity Temple. The Palace Museum documents a south-facing inscribed face. The heading aligns the apron with the visible path segment. The path link and the shelter footprint beneath the tree canopy remain approximate.

previousDraft.title: Summer Palace · Farming and Weaving Stele
previousDraft.note: The title faces due south in the draft. The two ground photos show the walk angled about 5 degrees east of the shelter axis. The anchor uses the west garden walk trial and remains provisional beneath the tree canopy.

terrainReference.basis: Terrarium height at the west-walk draft anchor, referenced to the calibrated paving clearance.

entry.title: Summer Palace · Farming and Weaving Stele
entry.note: Approximate, south-facing placement on the archival apron beside the west garden walk. The conservation account and photographs support adding the shelter over the same stele. The terrain-relative offset fits the paving to the sampled surface. Canopy limits absolute placement accuracy.

terrainReference.basis: Terrarium ground at the apron center meets the model at the recorded local height.

placedApron.basis: The archival rectangle sits west of the garden walk and north of its bend toward the temple. A pale edge remains visible there in the 2018 image. Ground photographs before and after sheltering show the same masonry wall near the title stone. The conservation account says the park built a shelter for this stone. Taken together, these support approximate continuity at the archival apron. The present roof outline and individual footings are obscured in overhead imagery.
placedApron.poseSource: Approximate anchor derived from the three aerial images of the open apron and the retained 2018 apron edge.
placedApron.headingSource: The inscribed face points south as documented by the Palace Museum and Beijing tourism archive.

postArchiveImages.observation: The north–south walk remains visible with a pale apron immediately on its west. Low resolution and branches obscure the central object.

An exposed pale edge projects west from the same garden-walk bend, north of the branch toward the temple. Its position agrees with the open apron in the 2005–2010 images. Canopy covers the western end.
The winter image locates the canal lock, temple and the path. The evergreen canopy at the apron leaves the roof less distinct than the garden controls.

continuitySources.observation: The account says the Summer Palace erected protective shelters for exposed monuments including the Farming and Weaving Stele starting in 2017.
The 2022 photo shows the covered stele beside the narrow east walk with a fieldstone wall behind the pavilion. The traveler approaches from the temple side.
The open and covered photographs show the round-headed slab, wave plinth and capped fieldstone wall. The open photograph capture date is unknown.
